blocks.prompt: 9 (i) Let \(f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\) be defined by \(f(x) = \frac{2x - 3}{x + 1}\). Find the domain and range of \(f(x)\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi Sawal 6 ki tarah fraction wala function hai, neeche \(x\) hai.
Diya kya hai? \(f(x) = \frac{2x - 3}{x + 1}\).
Find kya karna hai? Domain aur range.
Plan: neeche ko zero karne wala \(x\) hatana; \(y = f(x)\) ko \(x\) ke liye solve kar ke namumkin \(y\) dhoondna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(f(x) = \frac{2x - 3}{x + 1}\).
Humein find karna hai: domain aur range.
Tareeqa: Domain: \(x + 1 \ne 0\). Range: \(x\) ko \(y\) mein likh kar dekhna ke kaunsa \(y\) naye denominator ko zero karta hai; woh output kabhi nahi aata.

Domain
\[x + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -1\]
\[\text{Domain } f = \mathbb{R} - \{-1\}\]
Kyun: Zero se divide mumkin nahi. \(\mathbb{R} - \{-1\}\) ka matlab "saare real numbers siwaye \(-1\) ke".

\(y = f(x)\) ko \(x\) ke liye solve karein
\[y(x + 1) = 2x - 3\]
\[xy + y = 2x - 3\]
\[xy - 2x = -3 - y\]
\[x(y - 2) = -(y + 3)\]
\[x = \dfrac{y + 3}{2 - y}\]
Kyun: Fraction hatane ke liye \((x + 1)\) se multiply kiya, bracket khola, \(x\) wali terms baen taraf aur baqi daen taraf. \(x\) common nikaal kar \((y - 2)\) se divide kiya. Aakhir mein upar neeche \(-1\) se multiply kiya taake signs saaf hon; value nahi badli.

Namumkin output
\[2 - y = 0 \Rightarrow y = 2\]
\[\text{Range } f = \mathbb{R} - \{2\}\]
Kyun: \(y = 2\) par naya denominator zero hai, koi \(x\) nahi milta. Baqi har \(y\) ke liye real \(x\) milta hai, aur woh \(-1\) nahi hota (\(x = -1\) ke liye \(y + 3 = y - 2\) chahiye, yani \(3 = -2\), namumkin).
Shortcut yaad rakhein: range se \(\frac{2}{1} = 2\) (\(x\) ke coefficients ka ratio) nikalta hai.

Tasdeeq: kya 2 kabhi aata hai?
\[\dfrac{2x - 3}{x + 1} = 2\]
\[2x - 3 = 2x + 2 \Rightarrow -3 = 2\]
Kyun: Output 2 maan kar hal kiya to ghalat baat \(-3 = 2\) aayi. Matlab koi input 2 nahi deta. Range sahi hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Sawal mein \(f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\) likha hai, yani domain saare real numbers. Lekin \(f(-1) = \frac{-5}{0}\) defined hi nahi, is liye \(-1\) domain mein nahi ho sakta (kitab ka apna jawab bhi Domain \(\mathbb{R} - \{-1\}\) deta hai). Durust likhawat: \(f: \mathbb{R} - \{-1\} \to \mathbb{R}\). Teenon parts isi domain ke saath hal kiye gaye hain.

blocks.prompt: 9 (ii) Let \(f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\) be defined by \(f(x) = \frac{2x - 3}{x + 1}\). Determine whether \(f(x)\) is onto.
blocks.explanation:
Onto ka matlab: range bilkul co-domain ke barabar ho, yani co-domain ka har number kisi input se aaye.
Diya kya hai? Co-domain \(\mathbb{R}\), aur part (i) se range \(\mathbb{R} - \{2\}\).
Find kya karna hai? Kya \(f\) onto hai.
Plan: range aur co-domain ka muqabla, aur jo number reh gaya woh dikhana.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: co-domain \(\mathbb{R}\), Range \(f = \mathbb{R} - \{2\}\) (part (i) se).
Humein find karna hai: kya \(f\) onto hai.
Tareeqa: Onto ka matlab hai co-domain ke har element ka pre-image (woh input jis ka output yeh ho) mojood ho. Ek bhi number reh jaye to function onto nahi.

Muqabla karein
\[\text{Range } f = \mathbb{R} - \{2\} \ne \mathbb{R}\]
Kyun: 2 co-domain \(\mathbb{R}\) mein hai, lekin part (i) mein humne dekha ke koi \(x\) \(f(x) = 2\) nahi deta. Range mein ek "suraakh" hai.

Nateeja
Kyun: 2 ka koi pre-image nahi, is liye \(f\) onto \(\mathbb{R}\) nahi. Agar co-domain \(\mathbb{R} - \{2\}\) hota to yahi function onto hota; yani onto hona co-domain par munhasir hai.
Dhyan dein: "Onto nahi" kehne ke liye ek missing number dikhana zaroori hai; sirf "range chhoti hai" kehna adhoori daleel hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(f\) onto \(\mathbb{R}\) nahi, kyunke \(2 \in \mathbb{R}\) ka koi pre-image nahi (Range \(f = \mathbb{R} - \{2\}\)).

blocks.prompt: 9 (iii) Let \(f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\) be defined by \(f(x) = \frac{2x - 3}{x + 1}\). Prove that \(f(x)\) is one-to-one.
blocks.explanation:
Ab one-to-one saabit karna hai: barabar outputs se barabar inputs nikalne chahiye.
Diya kya hai? \(f(x) = \frac{2x - 3}{x + 1}\), domain se do inputs \(x_1, x_2\) (dono \(-1\) nahi).
Find kya karna hai? Proof ke \(f\) one-to-one hai.
Plan: \(f(x_1) = f(x_2)\) se cross-multiply, expand, cancel, aur \(x_1 = x_2\) tak pohanchna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(f(x) = \frac{2x - 3}{x + 1}\), \(x_1, x_2 \ne -1\).
Humein saabit karna hai: \(f(x_1) = f(x_2) \Rightarrow x_1 = x_2\).
Tareeqa: Do fractions barabar hon to cross-multiply kar sakte hain, bashart ke koi denominator zero na ho. Yahan \(x_1 + 1\) aur \(x_2 + 1\) zero nahi, kyunke dono inputs domain mein hain.

Barabar outputs se shuru karein
\[\dfrac{2x_1 - 3}{x_1 + 1} = \dfrac{2x_2 - 3}{x_2 + 1}\]
\[(2x_1 - 3)(x_2 + 1) = (2x_2 - 3)(x_1 + 1)\]
Kyun: \(\frac{p}{q} = \frac{r}{s}\) ho to \(ps = rq\). Is se fractions khatam ho gaye aur kaam aasaan ho gaya.

Dono taraf expand karein
\[2x_1x_2 + 2x_1 - 3x_2 - 3\]
\[= 2x_1x_2 + 2x_2 - 3x_1 - 3\]
Kyun: Ek bracket ki har term ko doosre bracket ki har term se multiply kiya. Baen: \(2x_1 \cdot x_2\), \(2x_1 \cdot 1\), \(-3 \cdot x_2\), \(-3 \cdot 1\). Daen bhi isi tarah.

Cancel aur jama karein
\[2x_1 - 3x_2 = 2x_2 - 3x_1\]
\[5x_1 = 5x_2\]
\[x_1 = x_2\]
Kyun: \(2x_1x_2\) aur \(-3\) dono taraf hain, cancel ho gaye. Phir dono taraf \(3x_1 + 3x_2\) jama kiya: baen \(5x_1\), daen \(5x_2\). 5 se divide kiya.
Dhyan dein: Expand karte waqt signs ka khayal; \(-3 \cdot x_2 = -3x_2\) aur \(-3 \cdot x_1 = -3x_1\) alag alag taraf hain.

Nateeja aur tasdeeq
\[f(0) = -3,\quad f(1) = -\tfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: Barabar outputs se barabar inputs nikle, is liye \(f\) one-to-one hai. Misaal se bhi: alag inputs 0 aur 1 ke outputs alag hain. Part (ii) ke saath: \(f\) one-to-one hai lekin onto \(\mathbb{R}\) nahi, is liye bijective nahi.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(f(x_1) = f(x_2) \Rightarrow x_1 = x_2\), is liye \(f\) one-to-one hai.
